item.description: sycl : vectorize reordered-layout dequantization stores (Q4_0, K-quants, IQ3, MXFP4) (#30976) * sycl : widen reordered q4_0 dequantization stores The reordered-layout Q4_0 conversion kernel processed one qs byte per work-item with two scalar stores, strided 16 elements apart. Give it the same treatment the Q8_0 kernel got in #30775: a flat sycl::range<1> launch with four qs bytes (8 outputs) per work-item inside one 32-element block and two vec stores. Same float math and rounding as the scalar kernel; output is bit-identical. The existing k % QK4_0 == 0 assert guarantees whole 32-element blocks, so the k/8 launch covers every row exactly. The now-unreferenced scalar reorder kernel is removed. Arc Pro B70, primed prefill (prefill after decode on a reorder-installed tensor): +6.4% to +7.3% pp512/pp2048 on Q4_0 models (tested up to 27B dense); fresh-layout prefill and decode unchanged; PPL within run noise. * sycl : vectorize reordered q4_K dequantization stores The reordered-layout Q4_K conversion kernel already loads its quantized inputs through sycl::vec but writes the dequantized results with scalar stores. Build the results in a vec register and emit two vector stores instead. Same per-element math; output is bit-identical. Arc Pro B70, primed prefill (prefill after decode on a reorder-installed tensor): +14.7% to +15.3% pp512/pp2048 on Q4_K-dominant models (tested up to 27B dense); fresh-layout prefill, decode and PPL unchanged. * sycl : remap reordered q5_K dequantization to vec4 loads/stores The reordered-layout Q5_K conversion kernel gave each thread only four outputs fed by scalar ql/qh byte loads plus a local-memory scale broadcast, so the stores were never its bottleneck: widening the stores alone measured within noise on mixed-quant models and +0.5% on a q5_K-dominant model. Re-decompose to 32 threads per block, each consuming four consecutive ql and qh bytes and emitting two aligned vec stores; a 4-element run shares one scale pair, so the per-element math and the output are identical. Arc Pro B70, primed prefill on a q5_K-dominant 27B model: +3.6% pp512/pp2048 over the scalar kernel; fresh-layout prefill, decode and PPL unchanged. The GET_ROWS reorder path moves to the same 32-thread decomposition. * sycl : remap reordered q6_K dequantization to vec4 stores The reordered-layout Q6_K conversion kernel wrote four scalars per thread, strided 32 elements apart, each pair of neighbors sharing neither instruction stream nor store transaction. Re-decompose the same 64-thread work-group so each thread emits one aligned vec : a 4-element run shares one 16-element scale group, one ql nibble source and one qh bit pair, so the per-element math and the output are identical to the scalar kernel. Arc Pro B70, primed prefill: +28.7% pp512/pp2048 on a Q6_K 27B model; fresh-layout prefill, decode and PPL unchanged. * sycl : vectorize reordered q3_K dequantization stores Each thread of the reordered-layout Q3_K conversion kernel already computes four consecutive outputs; build them in a vec register and emit one vector store instead of four scalars. Same per-element math; output is bit-identical. Arc Pro B70, primed prefill: +16.8% pp512/pp2048 on a Q3_K-dominant 27B model; fresh-layout prefill, decode and PPL unchanged. * sycl : vectorize reordered iq3_xxs/iq3_s dequantization stores Both reordered-layout IQ3 conversion kernels write eight contiguous outputs per thread as scalar stores (four from each grid lookup). Build two vec registers and emit two vector stores. Same per-element math; output is bit-identical. Arc Pro B70, primed prefill: +20.3% to +21.1% pp512/pp2048 on IQ3_XXS- and IQ3_S-dominant 27B models; fresh-layout prefill, decode and PPL unchanged. * sycl : remap reordered q2_K dequantization to vec4 stores Re-decompose the reordered-layout Q2_K conversion kernel the same way as Q6_K: one aligned vec per thread instead of four scalars strided 32 apart. A 4-element run shares one scale byte and one 2-bit lane, so the per-element math and the output are identical to the scalar kernel. Arc Pro B70, primed prefill: +13.1% pp512/pp2048 on a Q2_K-dominant 27B model; fresh-layout prefill, decode and PPL unchanged. * sycl : widen reordered mxfp4 dequantization stores Give the reordered-layout MXFP4 conversion kernel the same flat sycl::range<1> launch as Q4_0: four qs bytes (8 outputs) per work-item inside one 32-element block and two vec stores. item.description: common, mtmd: bound control vector layer indices and M-RoPE position loops (#31336) * common: bound control vector layer indices by the model layer count A direction tensor layer index is parsed from the tensor name with no upper bound, and the buffer size and write offset are computed in int. A large index overflows both, so the accumulation writes before the start of the buffer. Pass the model layer count to the loader, reject indices above it like the existing zero index check, and compute the sizes in size_t. * mtmd: fill M-RoPE positions by whole merge tiles The position loops of the Qwen-VL, GLM, PaddleOCR and Qwen2.5-VL encoders hardcode a 2x2 merge inside a stride of n_merge, so a patch grid that is not a multiple of the merge writes past the positions buffer. Iterate over whole merge tiles with n_merge inner steps, which bounds the writes by the patch count and gives the same positions on aligned grids. PaddleOCR also requires a merge aligned image at graph build, as the Qwen-VL family already does. **Website:** - **Attestations:** - **macOS/iOS:** - macOS Apple Silicon (arm64) - macOS Apple Silicon (arm64, KleidiAI enabled) DISABLED - macOS Intel (x64) - iOS XCFramework **Linux:** - Ubuntu x64 (CPU) - Ubuntu arm64 (CPU) - Ubuntu s390x (CPU) - Ubuntu 26.04 s390x (CPU) - Ubuntu 26.04 s390x (zDNN) - Ubuntu x64 (Vulkan) - Ubuntu arm64 (Vulkan) - Ubuntu x64 (CUDA 12) - CUDA 12.8 libraries - Ubuntu x64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 libraries - Ubuntu arm64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 libraries - Ubuntu x64 (ROCm 10.0) - Ubuntu x64 (OpenVINO) - Ubuntu x64 (SYCL FP32) - Ubuntu x64 (SYCL FP16) - Linux arm64 (Snapdragon: CPU, Adreno GPU, Hexagon NPU) - setup guide **Android:** - Android arm64 (CPU) - Android arm64 (Snapdragon: CPU, Adreno GPU, Hexagon NPU) - setup guide **Windows:** - Windows x64 (CPU) - Windows arm64 (CPU) - Windows arm64 (OpenCL Adreno) - Windows x64 (CUDA 12) - CUDA 12.4 DLLs - Windows x64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 DLLs - Windows arm64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 DLLs - Windows x64 (Vulkan) - Windows arm64 (Vulkan) - Windows x64 (OpenVINO) - Windows x64 (SYCL) - Windows x64 (ROCm 10.0) **openEuler:** - DISABLED - openEuler x86 (310p) - openEuler x86 (910b, ACL Graph) - openEuler aarch64 (310p) - openEuler aarch64 (910b, ACL Graph) **UI:** - UI

item.description: ## Overview This release adds the LiquidAI LFM3 family (text, vision, audio and omni) together with a new experimental streaming-audio API in mtmd, and wires realtime audio in and out of the server through the new /v1/realtime and /tts endpoints. A batch of new architectures landed: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, SenseNova U1, Beam, Kolibri-1, Flint, Muse Spark, Granite Switch Decision, plus decision/embedding models from LiquidAI, Baidu and NVIDIA. The core got sparse-attention (QSA/DSA) reworked onto a fused masking op, a 50/50 SLRU cache for host-resident MoE experts, and cleaner no_alloc memory handling; the server got router memory-management and tool-calling improvements; the UI can now browse and download models straight from HF Hub, search conversations and compact them. Finally, ggml was bumped to v0.28.0, bringing GGML_OP_TOP_K_MASK, -1 expert-index semantics and large backend performance work (CUDA chunked graph launches, SYCL graph replay, OpenCL Q2_K/Q3_K, item.description: tests : fix multi-seq split replay and partial-state cases for trained models (#31216) * tests : fix multi-seq split replay against trained models The rollback snapshot is captured by the graph that decoded the rolled-back tail, while the reference context decodes the same prefix with different batch shapes. Compare only the first replayed token of each seq, then restore the rollback state into the reference context before the seq-1-only tail. Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF (MacBook, M5 Max, 128GB) * tests : require bit-exact seq-1 isolation in split replay The seq state save is not always bit-lossless - SWA-masked cells are not saved - so reload the restored state back into the rollback context. That way both contexts enter the seq-1-only tail with byte-identical memory, including the cell layout, and the tail logits must match bit-exact. Also assert that the restored state round-trips bit-identical. item.description: common: pin model resolution on real HF repo layouts (#30548) * tests: pin model resolution on real repo listings Extend test-model-resolution with 63 repo listings captured verbatim from the HF API, chosen to cover every file naming pattern found across 1237 GGUF repos of the major publishers and pruned to whole quant groups. item.description: llama-quant : fix 4D tensor quantization using ggml_nrows() and name-based expert detection (#30820) * llama-quant : fix quantizing 4D tensors nrows_total was ne[1]*ne[2], so for a 4D tensor only the first ne[2] slices were quantized and the rest of the rows were dropped. Fixes #29916 * llama-quant : detect expert tensors by name and fix imatrix size for 4D tensors The MXFP4_MOE path used ne[2] > 1 to detect MoE expert tensors. This is wrong for non-expert tensors with 3 or more dims, e.g. MLA projections (BailingMoE3) and 4D conv kernels. Use the tensor name instead: all tensors used by GGML_OP_MUL_MAT_ID are named *_exps or *_chexps. This also removes the BailingMoE3 special case. The imatrix holds one vector of ne[0] values per 2D slice, so the expected size is ne[0]*ne[2]*ne[3], not ne[0]*ne[2]. This matches how the imatrix is indexed per row for 4D tensors in llama_tensor_quantize_impl. item.description: CUDA: fuse FFN gate/up matmuls and GLU in MMQ with interleaved gate/up rows (#29948) * cuda: fuse FFN gate/up and GLU in MMQ with interleaved gate/up rows For prompt processing, run the gate and up matmuls of a dense FFN as one mul_mat_q launch and apply the GLU in the write-back. - The loaders take the gate weights as a second pointer and fill the weight tile with up and gate rows interleaved in chunks of 8, so each thread holds an up value and the matching gate value (rows r and r + 8 of an MMA tile). - The MMA loop is unchanged: same tile, warp layout, vec_dot and one sum[] per thread. The fused write-back computes the GLU from registers and writes half the rows. - The fused path uses the regular tiling (no stream-k) with the column tiles innermost so that neighbouring blocks share weight tiles. -
